title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
abstract: arXiv:2611.14519v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within

translated_title: 医学图像分割：基础模型适配与任务专用训练的对比
translated_abstract: 在大规模自然图像集合上预训练的基础模型正日益被适配用于医学图像分割，人们期望它们能够取代针对每个任务单独训练的模型。然而，大多数比较研究使用的是来自训练分布的数据，且仅使用单一的、其配置鲜有合理依据的任务专用基线，因此对模型在新临床机构表现的评价证据有限。此外，基础模型需要适配多少参数、以及由什么因素决定这一程度，目前仍不清楚。我们采用从仅微调偏置项到全量微调等多种策略对基础模型DINOv2进行适配，并将其与从头训练的U-Net和ResU-Net进行比较。实验涵盖结肠镜、乳腺超声和皮肤镜图像，测试数据既包括来自训练源的留出数据，也包括来自其他机构的独立数据集。适配后的基础模型在每个外部数据集上都展现出更好的泛化能力。（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究将DINOv2基础模型以从仅调偏置项到全量微调的不同程度进行适配，并与从头训练的U-Net/ResU-Net在结肠镜、乳腺超声和皮肤镜分割任务上系统对比，证明适配后的基础模型在来自其他机构的独立外部数据集上具有更优的泛化能力。
en_tdlr: By adapting the DINOv2 foundation model with strategies ranging from bias-only tuning to full fine-tuning and comparing it against U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch on colonoscopy, breast ultrasound, and dermoscopy segmentation, this study demonstrates that the adapted foundation model generalizes better on every external dataset from unseen institutions.
